library-bees-deep-10: The bee does not have to plan to help the flower; its own food-gathering trip can make the transfer happen.
library-migration-deep-10: Several generations together complete the pattern that returns monarchs to their wintering places.
library-clouds-deep-11: New droplets form while others disappear, so it is an ongoing process rather than a fixed object.
library-rain-deep-10: Very large drops can break apart, so the familiar pointed teardrop is not the usual shape of falling rain.
library-wind-deep-10: Moving leaves and drifting clouds can trace air responding to pressure differences that our eyes cannot see directly.
library-water-cycle-deep-10: A diagram with one circle is useful, but a branching map with places to pause better matches the many possible journeys.
library-volcanoes-deep-10: A rock exposed by erosion may record underground magma rather than an eruption, even though both rocks began as molten material.
